The structure of a link-cut tree typically consists of a binary search tree where each node has a pointer to its parent, a pointer to its left and right children, and additional information to keep track of the tree's structure. To list the sizes of tables in a specific database using Microsoft SQL Server, you can use the `sys.dm_db_partition_stats` dynamic management view (DMV) along with `sys.tables`. The following query will help you achieve this:

```sql
USE YourDatabaseName;
GO

SELECT 
    t.name AS TableName,
    SUM(ps.used_pages) * 8 AS TableSizeKB
FROM 
    sys.tables AS t
    INNER JOIN 
    sys.dm_db_partition_stats AS ps ON t.object_id = ps.object_id
WHERE 
    t.type = 'U' -- U for user tables
GROUP BY 
    t.name
ORDER BY 
    TableSizeKB DESC;
```

Replace `YourDatabaseName` with the name of your database. This query will give you the table names along with their sizes in kilobytes, ordered from largest to smallest. The size is calculated by multiplying the used pages by 8 (since SQL Server pages are 8 KB in size).
